_comment: Titan's GHL workflow timing, mirrored from the live GHL automation settings so ghl-ingest-agent can predict staleness BEFORE the automation fires. Not secrets — version-controlled on purpose, so a change in GHL shows up as a reviewable diff here. Source: Albert, read from the GHL workflow UI 2026-07-25.
_maintenance: If a threshold changes in GHL, change it here in the same sitting. A stale value here makes ghl-ingest-agent's stale_approaching and abandonment_next findings silently wrong — worse than absent, because they look authoritative.

stale_thresholds_days._comment: Days in stage before GHL applies the `stale_lead` tag. Keys are EXACT live stage names, including prefixes and trailing spaces.

abandonment_rule._comment: Per the workflow: once `stale_lead` is present, if the same duration passes again the opportunity is automatically abandoned. So effective abandonment is 2x the stage threshold.

meeting_stage._comment: The Meeting-scheduled threshold counts from STAGE ENTRY, not from the appointment. An appointment booked far out eats into the window: a 30-day threshold with an appointment 10 days out leaves only ~20 days of post-appointment follow-up. There is no follow-up sequence for this stage yet — this is the window it must fit inside.

quote_followup_days._comment: Days after a mobile quote is sent that the follow-up text should fire (workflow step 7).

unstaged._comment: Stages with no stale threshold, and why. Do not invent thresholds for these.
unstaged.2. *Project Won*: terminal — deal closed, staleness is meaningless
unstaged.STORE: Material Pipeline: [FILL: thresholds not provided] — this pipeline runs its own +3d / +8d automated follow-up cadence and its stages were not covered in the workflow review. ghl-ingest-agent reports its volume but must NOT predict staleness here.
